transcript:
In the fabric library window, open the Pretty Files folder, and find A. Refining a jacket adding shoulder pads and sleeve hats in D. Fine Tuning.  
Flash the device on the file Refining a jacket or drag it into the 2D or 3D window. Using the Edit Pattern Piece tool, hold down the Shift key and select the armholes of the front and back pattern pieces. In the Property Editor, you can view the length of the selected 2D line segments.  
Select the Rectangle tool in the 2D toolbar. Right-click in the blank area of the 2D window, then left-click in the blank area of the 2D window. A dialog box will pop up; enter the height and width, then click.  
Use the Free Sewing tool to sew the newly created rectangle to the armhole. Using the Adjust Pattern Piece tool, right-click on the newly created pattern piece, select Client Linked Pattern Piece, Symmetrical Pattern Piece, Pattern Piece, and Sewing Line; hold down Shift and place the symmetrical pattern piece on the opposite side.  
Hold down the Shift key and select both rectangular pattern pieces. Right-click in the 3D window and select Add to Side from the pop-up menu.  
Place the facing strip pattern piece below the sleeve pattern piece, ensuring the facing strip is not placed below the sleeve pattern piece but not below the jacket body pattern piece.  
Activate simulation.  
Select the two rectangular pattern pieces.  
In the Property Editor, adjust the particle spacing to 5 and the collision thickness to 4.  
Activate simulation.  
Apply the footprint fabric property to the facing strip. In the Object window, add a fabric and apply it to both rectangular pattern pieces.  
In the Property Editor under Physical Property Mapping, select Trim Hardware.  
Activate simulation.  
Reset the ball joint.  
Press the curved facing.  
Configure around the curing machine.  
Configure around the curing machine.  
And place the texture map.  
Close.  
Good luck.  
Rotate.  
Rotate.

chunks.content: ## Adding Sleeve Plackets in CLO: Step-by-Step Fine-Tuning Tutorial This section explains the detailed process of adding sleeve plackets in CLO, focusing on pattern manipulation, sewing, fabric application, and simulation adjustments. Key tools include the Edit Pattern Piece tool, Rectangle tool, Free Sewing tool, and Property Editor settings. ### Opening and Preparing the Jacket Pattern - Open the **Fabric Library** window. - Navigate to the **Pretty Files** folder. - Locate the file titled **Refining a jacket adding shoulder pads and sleeve hats** in the **D. Fine Tuning** subfolder. - Load the file **Refining a jacket** by either double-clicking it or dragging it into the 2D or 3D window. ### Selecting Armholes and Measuring Lengths - Use the **Edit Pattern Piece** tool. - Hold down the **Shift** key and select the armholes of both the front and back pattern pieces. - Observe the length of the selected 2D line segments in the **Property Editor** for precise measurements. ### Creating the Sleeve Placket Rectangle - Select the **Rectangle** tool from the 2D toolbar. - Right-click once, then left-click once in the blank space of the 2D window to open the rectangle size dialog box. - Enter the desired **height and width** values for the sleeve placket rectangle. - Confirm by clicking the dialog box button to create the rectangle. ### Sewing and Mirroring the Pattern Piece - Use the **Free Sewing** tool to sew the newly created rectangle to the armhole edge. - Select the **Adjust Pattern Piece** tool. - Right-click the new rectangle and select the following options sequentially: - **Client Linked Pattern Piece** - **Symmetrical Pattern Piece** - **Pattern Piece** - **Sewing Line** - Hold **Shift** and place the symmetrical pattern piece on the opposite sleeve side to ensure mirroring. ### Aligning Pattern Pieces - Hold **Shift** and select both rectangular pattern pieces. - Right-click in the 3D window and choose **Add to Side** from the pop-up menu for proper positioning. ### Positioning the Facing Strip - Place the **facing strip** pattern piece underneath the sleeve pattern piece. - Ensure the facing strip is positioned below the sleeve but **not beneath the jacket body pattern piece** to maintain correct layering. ### Simulation and Physical Property Adjustments - Activate the simulation mode. - Select both rectangular pattern pieces. - In the **Property Editor**, adjust: - **Particle Spacing** to **5** - **Collision Thickness** to **4** - Reactivate simulation to apply these changes smoothly. ### Applying Fabric and Trim Hardware - Assign the **Footprint Fabric** property to the facing strip pattern piece. - In the **Object** window, add a fabric and apply it to both rectangular pattern pieces. - Under **Physical Property Mapping** in the Property Editor, select **Trim Hardware** to simulate hardware behavior on the plackets. - Activate simulation again to verify fabric and hardware effects. ### Final Adjustments - Reset the ball joint to ensure proper articulation. - Press and curve the facing piece to fit around the sleeve structure.
